title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as companies jockey for position in the burgeoning LEO market, while defense budgets are getting a notable boost. Meanwhile, the specter of hardware failures looms over the MEO sector, casting a shadow on the orbital economy's future.

themes.title: LEO Constellation Plans Emerge
themes.body: India's Jio is making waves with its sovereign LEO constellation plan, just in time for its IPO. This move signals a growing interest in LEO capabilities, as companies scramble to claim their stake in this lucrative market.

themes.title: M&A Activity Heats Up
themes.body: MDA Space's acquisition of Blue Canyon Technologies underscores the competitive landscape in the U.S. market. As companies consolidate, the pressure to innovate and scale becomes even more pronounced.

themes.title: Defense Budgets on the Rise
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, signaling a commitment to strengthening U.S. capabilities in space. This funding boost could accelerate development timelines for critical projects.

themes.title: MEO Hardware Concerns Grow
themes.body: The durability crisis facing MEO hardware raises questions about the sustainability of the new orbital economy. As operators grapple with potential failures, the industry must address these vulnerabilities to maintain investor confidence.
